Scope: User-selected Zimmerman ancillary maps and RECmd batch examples associated with the accepted 26-tool collection

Sources.PublisherRefresh: EvtxECmd --sync downloads current maps into the adjacent Maps folder
SQLECmd --sync downloads current maps into the adjacent Maps folder

Sources.PublisherCharacterization: README describes these as mostly community-maintained and says --sync updates local files

Findings: Each ancillary collection is separate from the tool executable versions and is mutable on its repository branch; a content refresh can change without a new tool release.

The published Get-ZimmermanTools -Sync implementation recursively discovers EvtxECmd, SQLECmd and RECmd executables under its destination and invokes each with --sync. Do not run it as part of package installation or staging.

EvtxECmd maps define event field extraction and descriptions; SQLECmd maps identify SQLite database types and queries; RECmd batches enumerate selected Registry keys/values. These are processing configuration, not tools, and their inclusion does not authorize processing evidence.
RECmd documentation says DFIRBatch.reb is also used by KAPE. This does not admit KAPE as a selected RIDE tool; exact batch inclusion and the KAPE relationship must be reviewed member by member.
SQLECmd 2026.10 documents that evidence databases are copied with WAL/journal files and only the copy is opened; this behavior is not acceptance evidence because SQLECmd was not run.
MigrationDisposition: Preserve the selected ancillary-content intent. Implement a separate explicit refresh workflow over pinned revisions with exact member inventory, compatibility, hashes, notices, custom-file preservation and recovery. Owner-specific license review markers are administrative and do not gate package migration.
Deferred: Resolve host network access to inspect current files and immutable commits
Enumerate selected map and batch members and retain upstream notices
Verify compatibility against exact tool versions and framework variants
Implement package-scoped explicit refresh with staging, modified-file conflict handling, ownership and recovery
